questions.questionText: Table 3 shows indices for the total revenue and total cost for a firm in the years 2021 to 2023, with 2022 set as the base year. In 2021, the firm’s total revenue was £180 000 and its total cost was £160 000. What was the firm’s total profit in 2023?
Table 2 shows an index of labour productivity per hour for a large car manufacturer. Which one of the following statements must be true?
options: Output per hour of labour was higher in 2017 than in 2021
Production of cars was higher in 2019 than in 2018
The firm was operating at full capacity in 2019
There were fewer workers employed in 2020 than in 2018

questions.questionText: Between 2021 and 2022, the weight applied to the restaurant and hotels sector in the Consumer Prices Index rose from 97 to 102. As a result of this change, it must be true that
options: average prices in the restaurant and hotels sector rose by just over 5% between 2021 and 2022.
restaurant and hotel prices rose by less than the overall average for consumer prices in 2021.
the proportion of average consumer expenditure relating to restaurants and hotels rose in 2022.
total consumer expenditure on restaurant and hotel services was higher in 2022 than in 2021.

questions.questionText: Table 2 shows the indices of labour productivity and real GDP for Country A and Country B for 2 years. Which one of the following can be concluded from the data?
options: In Year 2, labour productivity and real GDP were higher in Country A than Country B.
In Year 2, real GDP per capita was higher in Country A than Country B.
Labour productivity and real GDP grew more quickly in Country A than Country B over the period.
Real GDP per capita grew more quickly in Country A than in Country B.

questions.questionText: Table 8 shows an index of copper exports for a country during the years 2020 to 2023. Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: Between 2020 and 2023, the mean annual rate of growth in the country's exports of copper was 6%
In 2022, the country's exports of copper grew by 6.1%
The highest rate of growth in the country's exports of copper was in 2023
The rate of growth in the country's exports of copper was higher in 2021 than in 2022

questions.questionText: Table 9 shows the price index for an economy at the end of each of the years from 2019 to 2023. In which year did the economy experience disinflation?
Table 1 shows the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for an economy over a period of time. Which one of the following can be concluded from Table 1?
options: The price of a representative basket of goods rose throughout the period.
The rate of inflation from 2011 to 2014 was the same as from 2014 to 2017.
The standard of living reached its highest level in 2020.
The value of money rose between 2008 and 2011.

questions.questionText: Using the data in Extract A (Figure 1), if 2015 is the base year, calculate the index of Egypt’s real GDP in 2018. Give your answer to one decimal place.
The main reason that economic statistics are often expressed as index numbers is to
options: allow easier comparison of data.
calculate cost of living data.
convert nominal data to real data.
even out fluctuations in raw data.

questions.questionText: Index numbers for real GDP per head for Country X and Country Y, are shown in Table 1. From Table 1 it can be concluded that real GDP per head
options: grew at the same rate between 2018 and 2019 in both countries.
grew every year throughout the period in both countries.
rose faster in Country X between 2017 and 2019.
was higher in Country Y than in Country X from 2017 to 2019.

questions.questionText: Table 1 shows the individual price indices and the weightings of the three goods that make up a price index. What was the percentage increase in the overall price index between April 2021 to April 2022?
Table 4 shows the values of nominal GDP and a price index in two different years. What was the value of real GDP in 2019, to the nearest £ billion, expressed in 2015 prices?
options: £227 billion
£261 billion
£264 billion
£319 billion

questions.questionText: The index of real GDP for an economy was 100 in 2017, its base year, and 105 in 2020. In 2017, real GDP was £500 billion. The monetary value of real GDP for this economy in 2020 must therefore have been
options: £395 billion.
£475 billion.
£525 billion.
£605 billion.

questions.questionText: Table 4 shows the weights used in the Consumer Prices Index (CPI) for a selection of items in 2008 and 2018. The data in Table 4 indicate that between 2008 and 2018 the
options: average price of goods fell, whereas the average price of services increased.
percentage increase in the price of ‘Clothing and footwear’ was greater than the percentage increase in the price of ‘Transport’.
proportion of total expenditure, by a typical household, on ‘Alcoholic beverages and tobacco’ did not change.
total expenditure of a typical household on ‘Food and non-alcoholic beverages’ fell.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements about the consumer price index (CPI) is correct?
options: A fall in the CPI means that the real value of money is falling
An increase in the CPI means that the rate of inflation is rising
The CPI measures changes in the prices of goods and services bought by households
The weights used in the CPI reflect changes in the quality of goods and services

questions.questionText: Table 1 shows the index of export prices, the current monetary value of a country’s exports and the calculated value, to the nearest £ billion, of the value of its exports at 2017 prices. Which one of the following is correct?
options: The value of the country’s exports in 2016 at 2017 prices, to the nearest £ billion, was £162 billion
The value of the country’s exports in 2016 at 2017 prices, to the nearest £ billion, was £198 billion
The value of the country’s exports in 2019 at 2017 prices, to the nearest £ billion, was £240 billion
The value of the country’s exports in 2019 at 2017 prices, to the nearest £ billion, was £250 billion

questions.questionText: The following table shows real GDP for a small economy over two years. If 2016 is the base year, the index number for real GDP in 2015, to the nearest whole number, would be
An economy’s GDP increased from £400 billion in 2016 to £428 billion in 2018. Using 2016 as the base year, what is the value of the index for GDP in 2018?
The table below shows the index of real GDP for the UK before and after the 2008–09 financial crisis. From the data it can be inferred that in the UK
options: real GDP fell by 2.5% between 2007 and 2011.
the annual rate of inflation was minus 1.1% in 2008.
the rate of economic growth was lower in 2011 than in 2010.
total output of the economy fell by 5.2% between 2007 and 2009.

questions.questionText: Changes are regularly made to the weights used in the UK’s Consumer Prices Index. This means that the index takes account of changes in
options: month on month increases in the general price level.
spending patterns throughout the economy.
the growth of real output in the economy.
total spending on all domestic goods and services.

questions.questionText: The following table shows the real GDP of an economy from 2012 to 2016. If the figures were converted to index form with 2013 as the base year, what would be the value of the index (to the nearest whole number) in 2016?
The table below shows the Consumer Prices Index for a country over a number of years. Which one of the following can be concluded from the table?
options: The country suffered disinflation in Year 5
The inflation rate was highest in Year 7
The only time the country suffered deflation was in Year 2
Real incomes fell between Year 1 and Year 7

questions.questionText: The table below shows how the index of GDP and the index of population changed in an economy between 2011 and 2015. Which one of the following can be inferred from the data?
options: Population was higher than GDP in 2011
Between 2011 and 2013, GDP grew by 8% whereas population grew by 3%
There was no growth in GDP per capita between 2013 and 2015
Money GDP increased by more than real GDP between 2011 and 2015
